questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol. It is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web, used to transfer web pages from servers to browsers.

questions.question: Which network topology uses a central hub or switch to connect all devices?
questions.explanation: In a Star topology, all devices connect to a central hub or switch. It is the most commonly used topology in modern networks. If the central hub fails, the entire network goes down.

questions.question: Which type of network covers the largest geographical area?
questions.explanation: WAN (Wide Area Network) covers the largest geographical area — spanning cities, countries, or even continents. The Internet is the largest WAN. LAN covers a small area (e.g., home/office), MAN covers a city.

questions.question: Which network device is used to connect two different networks and route data between them?
questions.explanation: A Router connects two or more networks (e.g., your home network to the Internet) and routes data packets between them. A Hub broadcasts to all devices. A Switch connects devices within the same network.

questions.question: What does SMTP stand for?
questions.explanation: SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. It is used to send emails from a client to a server, or between email servers. POP3/IMAP are used to receive emails.

questions.question: Which protocol is used for secure web browsing (encrypted HTTP)?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) encrypts data transfer between the browser and server using SSL/TLS. The padlock icon in the browser address bar indicates HTTPS is being used.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a firewall in a network?
options: To speed up the internet connection
To monitor and control incoming/outgoing network traffic
To assign IP addresses to devices
questions.explanation: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic based on predefined security rules. It acts as a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks.

questions.question: What does IP address stand for?
questions.explanation: IP stands for Internet Protocol. An IP address is a unique numerical label assigned to every device on a network, used for device identification and location addressing.

questions.question: What is cloud computing?
options: Delivery of computing services (servers, storage, databases) over the internet
questions.explanation: Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of computing services — including servers, storage, databases, networking, software — over the internet ('the cloud'). Examples: Google Drive, AWS, Azure.

questions.question: In a bus topology, if the main cable (backbone) fails, what happens?
options: Only the devices near the break are affected
Only the end devices are affected
questions.explanation: In bus topology, all devices share a single backbone cable. If this cable fails or breaks, the entire network stops working — this is the main disadvantage of bus topology.
